# YouTube Ads for Local Businesses: How to Reach Nearby Customers Before They Search

October 15, 2026 • Heights Digital

**Quick answer:** YouTube ads let a local business put short video in front of people in a specific service area, and with skippable in-stream ads you generally pay only when someone watches long enough or interacts. They work best for building familiarity and demand before people search, and for retargeting website visitors. Start with a 15 to 60 second ad that hooks in the first five seconds, target your area tightly, and measure by branded search lift and leads, not just views.

Most small businesses think of YouTube ads as something for national brands. But YouTube lets you target by ZIP code or radius, and much of YouTube viewing now happens on TVs at home. That means a roofing company, med spa or law firm can run what is effectively a local TV commercial, aimed only at its service area, with clear reporting. This guide covers how to do it without wasting money.

## What YouTube ads are good for

*   **Getting known before people need you.** When someone's water heater fails, they call the name they recognize.
*   **Retargeting.** Showing video to people who visited your site but didn't call.
*   **Explaining complex or expensive services** that need more than a headline.
*   **Recruiting,** by putting a short "work with us" video in front of local job seekers.

YouTube ads generally aren't the best tool for capturing someone who needs help right now. That's what Google Search and Local Services Ads are for. Use them together. Our [Google Ads guide](https://heightsdigitalmedia.com/pages/blog/google-ads-for-small-business-honest-guide) covers the search side.

## The main YouTube ad formats

*   **Skippable in-stream:** plays before or during videos, skippable after five seconds. You typically pay when someone watches 30 seconds (or the whole ad if it's shorter) or clicks. The workhorse format for small businesses.
*   **Non-skippable in-stream:** short ads viewers must watch. Good for a tight message, but you pay for impressions.
*   **Bumper ads:** six-second non-skippable ads. Good reminders, too short to explain much.
*   **In-feed video ads:** appear in YouTube search results and recommendations. Useful when people are searching topics related to your service.
*   **Shorts ads:** vertical ads shown between Shorts. Your Reels-style content can work here.

Google also offers campaign types like Demand Gen and Performance Max that can place video on YouTube alongside other placements. Those are useful, but a dedicated video campaign gives you clearer control when you're starting.

## Targeting a local audience

1.  **Location:** set your service area by radius or ZIP codes, using "presence" so you reach people physically in the area.
2.  **Customer lists and website visitors:** retarget past visitors and upload customer lists for similar audiences.
3.  **Custom segments:** audiences built from people who have searched certain terms on Google, such as "roof replacement" or "Invisalign."
4.  **Life events and in-market audiences:** people moving, buying a home, or actively researching your category.
5.  **Content and placements:** optional, such as showing on home improvement or local news channels.

Avoid stacking too many layers on a small area. You'll shrink your audience until the ads barely deliver.

## What makes a YouTube ad work

The first five seconds decide everything, because that's when viewers can skip.

*   **Lead with the viewer's problem or your brand in the first five seconds.** If they skip, they at least saw who you are.
*   **Show a real person and real work.** Owners and technicians build more trust than voiceovers over stock footage.
*   **Keep it 15 to 60 seconds** for most local ads.
*   **One message, one call to action.** "Schedule your free inspection" with your website or phone number on screen.
*   **Design for TV and phone.** Big readable text, clear audio, and a horizontal version for TV plus a vertical cut for Shorts.

If you're considering broader TV-style placements, our post on [streaming TV ads for local businesses](https://heightsdigitalmedia.com/pages/blog/ctv-streaming-tv-ads-for-local-business) compares the options, and our [commercial video guide](https://heightsdigitalmedia.com/pages/blog/commercial-video-for-small-business) covers production.

# How Much Do YouTube Ads Cost? Complete Pricing Breakdown

[YouTube advertising](https://www.edgedigital.net/services/youtube-ads/) is a super effective way to reach new customers. But figuring out the costs can be a bit confusing when you’re just getting started. This guide breaks down what you will actually pay, based on what we see running [YouTube ads management](https://www.edgedigital.net/services/youtube-ads/) for our own clients.

**YouTube ads usually cost between £0.008-£0.024 per view.** So, reaching 100,000 viewers could run you about £800-£2,400. That’s pretty affordable compared to most advertising platforms.

The actual price depends on things like your target audience, ad format, and how competitive your industry is. YouTube uses an auction system, so you only pay when people interact with your ad.

This setup gives you a lot of control over your spending and helps you get the most out of your budget.

Let’s break down what you need to know about YouTube ad costs, from pricing models to budget strategies. Whether you’re running your first campaign or trying to get more from your ad spend, knowing these numbers will help you plan better.

![youtube ad costs 2026 infographic](https://www.edgedigital.net/wp-content/uploads/YouTube-Ad-Costs-2026-Infographic.png "How Much Do YouTube Ads Cost? Complete Pricing Breakdown")

### Key Takeaways

*   YouTube ads cost between £0.008-£0.024 per view, with daily budgets starting from £8.
*   Different ad formats (skippable, non-skippable, bumper ads) have different costs.
*   Your costs depend on targeting, bidding, and industry competition.

## How Much Do YouTube Ads Cost in 2026?

YouTube advertising costs in 2026 are usually between £0.04 and £0.25 per view. Most businesses start with daily budgets as low as £8, and spend anywhere from £8 to £40 per day.

### Average YouTube Ad Pricing

The [cost of YouTube ads in 2026](https://www.evendigit.com/youtube-ad-costs-2025-breakdown/) depends on how you pay. Cost Per View (CPV) rates are usually £0.04 to £0.25, and Cost Per Click (CPC) ranges from £0.80 to £2.40.

Cost Per Thousand Impressions (CPM) is typically between £3.20 and £12.00. That’s pretty competitive with other digital platforms.

**Pricing Model Breakdown:**

*   **CPV:** £0.04 – £0.25
*   **CPC:** £0.80 – £2.40
*   **CPM:** £3.20 – £12.00
*   **CPA:** £8.00 – £40.00

TrueView skippable ads are the most affordable at £0.04 to £0.08 per view. Non-skippable ads cost more, around £8.00 to £16.00 CPM, since people have to watch the whole thing.

### Typical Budget Ranges for Advertisers

[Daily YouTube ad spending](https://www.evendigit.com/youtube-ad-costs-2025-breakdown/) really depends on your business size and goals. Small businesses usually spend £400 to £1,600 per month.

**Budget Ranges by Business Size:**

| Business Type | Monthly Budget | Daily Spend |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Small Business | £400 – £1,600 | £13 – £53 |
| Mid-sized Company | £2,400 – £8,000 | £80 – £267 |
| Enterprise | £8,000+ | £267+ |

Starting with at least £400 a month is a good idea to get enough data for testing and tweaking your ads.

Most campaigns need 2-4 weeks of testing before you’ll see the best results. Make sure your budget covers this learning period.
